answer.text:
The master-data assessment written up by Tomas Lindholm on 2 May 2024 reported four conclusions and no completion claims: ECC 6.0 was fine with no concerns about the nightly batch for daily replenishment; DC-2 was entered as a named risk (out-of-support middleware, intermittent failure, silent mode) with monitoring to be designed around it from day one; master data needed a remediation workstream owned on Acme's side, with case pack quantity identified as the blocking gap; and remaining shelf life was left as an open question — whether it is obtainable outside the WMS — which Lindholm wanted answered in May 2024 rather than 2025. The assessment was a findings document and reported nothing as complete. [1]

What was reported in September 2024 came from the master data workshop of 24 September 2024, not from the assessment. Kwame Boateng reported the first-extract findings: case pack quantity missing on 31 percent of active articles (Priya Nair noted she had estimated a third); store master clean; product hierarchy clean; supplier lead times populated but not believed, because many were exactly seven days; and shelf life populated on 48 percent. [2] [3] [4] [5] [6]

At the same workshop Boateng stated what blocked the phase: case pack blocks ordering, because you cannot order in units the supplier does not ship; lead times affect accuracy rather than function; and shelf life does not block anything for this phase because fresh is not in it. For the pilot cohort — not the whole range — he gave an approximate size of about 4,200 articles, of which roughly 1,300 lacked case pack (the transcript turn is cut off mid-figure, so the roughly-1,300 figure is approximate and incomplete in the record). [7] [8] [9] [10] [11] [12]

The remediation itself was not complete in September 2024. The scope was set out in Kwame Boateng's 30 September 2024 email: 4,214 articles in the pilot cohort, 1,317 missing case pack quantity, 3,105 missing or default supplier lead times, and shelf life populated at 48 percent. Case pack was named the blocker, lead times could be worked around by deriving actuals from receipt history, and shelf life was out of scope for the phase. An attachment with the 1,317 articles is referenced; its contents are not in the supplied record. [13]

Progress was reported later: 780 of 1,317 case pack values done after four weeks (Priya Nair, 28 October 2024), with two unresponsive suppliers accounting for about 200 articles; and completion of all 1,317 on 19 December 2024, with the two unresponsive suppliers resolved by measuring actual delivered quantities over six months and inferring the case pack — correct for 190 of the 200 affected articles. [14] [15]

At the 21 January 2025 UAT readiness review Priya Nair confirmed case pack for the cohort was done (about thirteen hundred articles, finished 19 December), that lead times had not been touched and were still mostly sevens, and that shelf life was untouched and not in scope, with the warehouse question still unanswered. [16] [17] [18] [19]

The 48 percent shelf-life figure appears in both the 24 September 2024 workshop and the 30 September 2024 scope email, and it remained unchanged through the phase: Ana Duarte recorded in the steering report on 20 December 2024 that shelf life remained at 48 percent and untouched, correct for this phase and expected to become the critical path for phase two. [6] [13] [20]

Distinguishing the two: the May 2024 assessment reported findings and an open question, not completions; the September 2024 workshop reported measured data-quality figures (31 percent missing case pack, 48 percent shelf life populated, clean store master and hierarchy, unreliable lead times) and identified the blocking gap; and remediation completion of all 1,317 case pack values was only reported in December 2024. [1] [2] [6] [15]

Priya,

Assessment written up as promised. Four conclusions.

ECC 6.0 is fine and we have no concerns about the nightly batch for daily replenishment.

DC-2 goes in as a named risk. Out of support middleware, intermittent failure, silent
mode. We will design monitoring around it from day one rather than assume it works.

Master data needs a remediation workstream owned on your side. Case pack quantity is the
blocking gap.

The open question from our call: is remaining shelf life obtainable? You said the total
sits on the article and the arrival date is in the warehouse system. Could you find out
whether that is exposed outside the WMS? It changes the phase two design and I would
rather know in May 2024 than in 2025.

Med vänliga hälsningar,
Tomas Lindholm

Confirmed the 2 May 2024 assessment email contains four conclusions, no completion claims, and leaves shelf life as an open question.
Confirmed the 24 September 2024 workshop figures (31% missing case pack, clean store master and hierarchy, lead times not believed, 48% shelf life populated) across utterances 14, 16, 17, 19 and 25.

Noted the workshop cohort figure is fragmented: utterance 37 gives about 4,200 and utterance 40 is cut off mid-sentence, so the roughly-1,300 missing-case-pack figure is qualified as approximate and incomplete in the transcript.

Confirmed the 30 September 2024 scope email figures (4,214 / 1,317 / 3,105 / 48%) and that shelf life is out of scope; noted the attachment with the 1,317 is referenced but its contents are not in the supplied record.

Confirmed remediation progress (780 of 1,317 on 28 October 2024) and completion (all 1,317 on 19 December 2024, inference method correct for 190 of 200) are dated after September, so remediation completion is kept separate from the September findings.
